code: parse_jobs_ini() begins parsing attacker-supplied INI job text
note: The raw job-file input is accepted as configuration text and handed to the INI parser.

code: __parse_jobs_ini(...) iterates over sections and options in the parsed job file
note: The description option from the INI file is preserved for later option handling.
The parser passes the collected option strings into the option-substitution path.

code: dup_and_sub_options(char **opts, int num_opts) duplicates and substitutes option strings
note: Each option string is duplicated and then scanned for keyword substitutions before being stored.
The description value "$ncpus" is examined for a built-in keyword replacement.

code: fio_keywords[] contains the "$ncpus" keyword and its runtime replacement string
note: The replacement text length is derived from runtime system information and can be larger than the input token.

code: keyword expansion copies the replacement into the option buffer
note: The expansion path writes the replacement into memory sized for the original option text, creating the suspected heap overrun when the replacement outgrows the token.
